records.title: Limit
records.definition: A limit describes the value a function or sequence approaches as its input approaches a specified value or as an index grows.
principles: Limits provide the foundation for derivatives and integrals.
relationships: Limits connect functions, continuity, derivatives and integrals.
misconceptions: A limit does not always equal the function value at the point.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions

records.title: Derivative
records.definition: A derivative describes the instantaneous rate of change of a function with respect to its input.
principles: A derivative is defined using a limit of a difference quotient.
relationships: Derivatives connect functions, limits, motion and optimization.
misconceptions: A derivative is not simply the slope of one fixed straight line.
questions: How is a derivative related to a limit?
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; NIST mathematical-functions reference

records.title: Integral
records.definition: An integral is used to represent accumulation and, in definite form, can represent signed area under a curve.
principles: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus connects differentiation and integration.
relationships: Integrals connect derivatives, area, volume and probability.
examples: The integral of x is x^2/2 + C.
misconceptions: An integral is not always simply geometric area above the x-axis.
questions: How are derivatives and integrals connected?
assessment_ideas: Evaluate basic indefinite and definite integrals.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; NIST mathematical-functions reference
